old_digest: Shall stand at a reasonable distance behind the wicket, and shall not move till the ball is out of the bowler’s hand, and shall not, by any noise, incommode the striker; and if his hands, knees, foot, or head, be over or before the wicket, though the ball hit it, it shall not be out.
new_digest: Shall stand at a reasonable distance behind the Wicket and shall not move till the Ball is out of the Bowler’s Hand, and shall not by any Noise incommode the Striker, and if his Hands, Knees, Foot or Head be over or before the Wicket, though the Ball touch it, it shall not be out.

old_digest: They are the sole judges of fair and unfair play, and all disputes shall be determined by them When a striker is hurt, they are to allow another to come in, and the person hurt shall have his place in any part of that innings. But if the bowler’s foot is not behind the bowling-crease, and within the return-crease, when he delivers the ball, the umpire, unasked, must call no ball.

old_digest: If the striker moves out of his ground to strike at the ball, he shall be allowed no notch for such stroke, unless he returns to his ground after he has struck the ball.
But if the party goes in a second time, then the bet must be determined by the number on the score.

old_digest: Must be twenty-two inches, and the bail six inches long; but by a subsequent meeting it is settled for to use three stumps instead of two, to each wicket, and the two bails not to exceed six inches.
